content.overview: Section 12 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 provides that an adopted child is deemed to be the child of his or her adoptive father or mother for all purposes with effect from the date of the adoption. All ties with the family of birth are severed, subject to the provisos: the child cannot marry any person whom he or she could not have married if he or she had continued in the family of birth; any property vested before adoption continues with the child subject to obligations attached to it; and the adoptive family is not divested of property vested in it before the adoption.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Valid adoption under s. 6? (2) Child of adoptive parents from date of adoption? (3) Ties with birth family severed? (4) Marriage, vested property, and non-divesting provisos?
content.study:
Section 12 operates only if the adoption is valid under s. 6 and the Chapter.

Main effects: transplantation into the adoptive family; severance of birth-family ties (subject to provisos).

Provisos protect prohibited degrees for marriage, vested property of the child, and property already vested in the adoptive family.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Deemed child of adoptive parents
sections.body: From the date of adoption the child is deemed the child of the adoptive father or mother for all purposes.

sections.heading: Severance of birth ties
sections.body: Ties with the family of birth are deemed to be severed and replaced by those of the adoptive family.

sections.heading: Marriage proviso
sections.body: Child cannot marry any person whom he or she could not have married in the family of birth.

sections.heading: Vested property of child
sections.body: Property vested in the child before adoption continues to vest, subject to obligations attached to it.

sections.heading: Non-divesting of adoptive family
sections.body: Adoption does not divest any person of property already vested in the adoptive family before the adoption.

examples.title: Severance
examples.body: Valid adoption — child becomes child of adoptive parents; birth-family ties severed subject to provisos.

hypotheticals.question: Does adoption automatically take away property already vested in the adoptive family’s other members?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The third proviso protects property vested in the adoptive family before the adoption.

misconceptions.trap: Adoption severs all ties including prohibited degrees for marriage.
misconceptions.correction: The first proviso preserves the birth-family prohibited degrees for marriage.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the effects of adoption under HAMA s. 12.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Deemed child; severance; three provisos on marriage, child’s vested property, and adoptive family’s vested property.
